equivalent_survivor_proofs.mutation: shoelace second index i+1 changed to i+0 or i*1
equivalent_survivor_proofs.proof: For a regular n-gon, write vertex i as c + R(cos(theta_i), sin(theta_i)) with theta_(i+1)=theta_i+delta. Translation terms cancel. The original signed double area is n*R^2*sin(delta); either mutant is n*R^2*sin(delta)/2. For n>=3 both expressions have exactly the same zero status, finiteness class, and sign used by P9.

equivalent_survivor_proofs.mutation: signed area greater-than zero changed to greater-than-or-equal
equivalent_survivor_proofs.proof: The immediately preceding guard rejects signed_double_area == 0.0, so > 0.0 and >= 0.0 are identical on every continuing execution.

equivalent_survivor_proofs.mutation: edge length less-than-or-equal zero changed to equality
equivalent_survivor_proofs.proof: math.hypot is nonnegative. Therefore length <= 0.0 if and only if length == 0.0.

equivalent_survivor_proofs.mutation: half-angle endpoint inequality changed to equality
equivalent_survivor_proofs.proof: The clamped cosine lies in [-1, 1], so acos(cosine)/2 lies in [0, pi/2]. Within that closed range, <= 0 equals == 0 and >= pi/2 equals == pi/2.

equivalent_survivor_proofs.mutation: corner sweep >= pi changed to > pi
equivalent_survivor_proofs.proof: For a regular n-gon with n>=3, the canonical sweep magnitude is 2*pi/n. It is positive and strictly less than pi; equality would require n=2, which the polygon contract rejects.

equivalent_survivor_proofs.mutation: overlap test > changed to >= at half-edge plus tolerance
equivalent_survivor_proofs.proof: The validated public contract requires corner_radius <= circumradius/2. The P9 non-overlap proof gives tangent_distance <= half_edge, which is strictly below half_edge + 1e-9. Both comparisons are false for every in-domain polygon.

equivalent_survivor_proofs.mutation: corner join index < length changed to != length
equivalent_survivor_proofs.proof: enumerate(corners) yields exactly 0 <= index < len(corners). Thus index+1 < len(corners) if and only if index+1 != len(corners). The 300-side witness separately kills identity-based substitutions.
RegularPolygonDrawingComponent validates corner_radius in [0, radius/2], and raster reconstructs that value before allocation. On a nonnegative domain, > 0.0 and != 0.0 are identical.
The same validated corner-radius domain is nonnegative, so == 0.0 and <= 0.0 select the same sharp polygons.
Canonical regular-polygon corners have sweep magnitude 2*pi/n for n>=3, so sweep is never zero. Greater-than and greater-than-or-equal therefore select the same direction.
